newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore's Lee apologises for offence to Malaysia.
newsitem.headline: Singapore's Lee apologises for offence to Malaysia.

text.p: Singapore Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew has apologised unreservedly for the offence he caused by a statement he made about a Malaysian state, his press secretary said on Thursday.

"The Senior Minister had no intention to cause offence and apologises unreservedly for the offence he has caused to the government and people of Malaysia by his statement on Johor," a statement by Lee's press secretary said.
Lee, Singapore's Prime Minister from 1959 to 1990, had said in a legal affadavit related to a libel case that Malaysia's Johor was "notorious for shootings, muggings and car-jackings".
The Malaysian foreign ministry on Wednesday demanded an apology and a retraction of the remark, and on Thursday Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said Lee should make amends for the comments.
The statement on Thursday from Lee's press secretary said Lee had not been to Johor since 1990 and his comments reflected "his perception based on reports he had read in the press".
